About the Billabong Cove

At 16' wide, the Billabong Cove is one of the broadest shapes in the Barrier Reef range, and its curves make that width feel relaxed rather than formal. Choose it when you'd rather have a pool that looks like part of the landscape than a straight-edged centerpiece.

The lounging ledge gives you somewhere to sit in shallow water, and the deep-end lounge seating gives you a second place to settle at the other end. Palms, natural stone and planting beds all work well around its outline, which is one reason freeform shells suit so many Northeast Florida yards.

Who is the Billabong Cove best for?

Homeowners who want a natural, resort feel and have space for planting around the pool.

How much yard does the Billabong Cove need?

As a first estimate, allow about 44' by 24' for the Billabong Cove, which adds a 4-foot walkway on each side. Your setbacks, easements and deck plans decide the real limit, and we confirm them on the free site visit.

Billabong Cove questions

The Billabong Cove suits a larger yard better. It is 35'3" by 16', before you allow for a deck and setbacks. iTop Pools measures your yard on a free site visit and confirms whether it fits.

The Billabong Cove holds about 17,400 gallons. These figures come from Barrier Reef Pools USA.

The Billabong Cove goes from 3'4" to 6'5".

The Billabong Cove has a lounging area, but no built-in spa. Ask iTop Pools about adding a separate one.
